Research has established the Social Learning Program as the ""treatment of choice"" for individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders in inpatient treatment settings. It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community.
cond_0001.responsibilities: The Social Learning Program is looking for a Psychologist with training and experience working with individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders. The Psychologist will function as an active member of an interdisciplinary treatment team. cond_0090.intro: The Social Learning Program at [Company name masked] is the longest running program of its kind in the nation. Research has established the Social Learning Program as the ""treatment of choice"" for individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders in inpatient treatment settings. It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community.
cond_0090.responsibilities: The Social Learning Program is looking for a Psychologist with training and experience working with individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders. The Psychologist will work as an active member of an interdisciplinary treatment team. In addition to contributing to milieu-based services, the Psychologist will coordinate with the team to deliver a range of clinical interventions, including individual and group psychotherapy and clinical case management, which they will then document. They will also share observational assessment data with the treatment team to support data-driven case conceptualization, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making. They may conduct psychological assessments as needed. While Social Learning Programs are a recognized evidence-based practice in and of themselves, they can also incorporate additional evidence-based practices to meet the individual needs and functioning of clients; therefore, the Psychologist is encouraged to keep abreast of existing and emerging evidence-based practices so they can be considered for implementation in collaboration with the team. Psychologists who are creative, detail-oriented, and dedicated to the delivery of evidence-based treatment would be well suited to this position.

cond_0159.intro: The Social Learning Program at [Company name masked] is the longest running program of its kind in the nation. Research has established the Social Learning Program as the ""treatment of choice"" for individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders in inpatient treatment settings. It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community.
cond_0159.responsibilities: The Social Learning Program is looking for a Psychologist with training and experience working with individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders. The Psychologist will function as an active, engaged member of an interdisciplinary treatment team, regularly communicating and collaborating with colleagues across disciplines. In addition to providing milieu-based services, the Psychologist will utilize a range of clinical interventions, including individual and group psychotherapy and clinical case management, which they will then document. They will also utilize observational assessment data to assist the treatment team with data-driven case conceptualization, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making, actively contributing to team discussions and speaking up when clinical concerns arise. They may conduct psychological assessments as needed. While Social Learning Programs are a recognized evidence-based practice in and of themselves, they can also incorporate additional evidence-based practices to meet the individual needs and functioning of clients; therefore, the Psychologist is encouraged to keep abreast of existing and emerging evidence-based practices so they can be considered for implementation, and to initiate discussions with the team about practices worth exploring. Psychologists who are creative, detail-oriented, and dedicated to the delivery of evidence-based treatment would be ideally suited to this position.

cond_0231.intro: The Social Learning Program at [Company name masked] is the longest running program of its kind in the nation. Research has established the Social Learning Program as the ""treatment of choice"" for individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders in inpatient treatment settings. It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community.
cond_0231.responsibilities: The Social Learning Program is looking for a Psychologist with training and experience working with individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders. The Psychologist will function as an active, engaged member of an interdisciplinary treatment team, regularly communicating and collaborating with colleagues across disciplines. In addition to providing milieu-based services, the Psychologist will utilize a range of clinical interventions, including individual and group psychotherapy and clinical case management, which they will then document. They will also utilize observational assessment data to assist the treatment team with data-driven case conceptualization, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making, actively contributing to team discussions and speaking up when clinical concerns arise. They may conduct psychological assessments as needed. While Social Learning Programs are a recognized evidence-based practice in and of themselves, they can also incorporate additional evidence-based practices to meet the individual needs and functioning of clients; therefore, the Psychologist is encouraged to keep abreast of existing and emerging evidence-based practices so they can be considered for implementation, and to initiate discussions with the team about practices worth exploring. Psychologists who are creative, detail-oriented, and dedicated to the delivery of evidence-based treatment would be ideally suited to this position.

Doctorate in Psychology
License eligible or licensed as a Psychologist
Training and/or experience treating individuals diagnosed with serious mental illnesses

Research has established the Social Learning Program as the ""treatment of choice"" for individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders in inpatient treatment settings. It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community.
cond_0323.responsibilities: The Social Learning Program is looking for a Psychologist with training and experience working with individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders. The Psychologist will function as an active member of an interdisciplinary treatment team. In addition to delivering milieu-based services, the Psychologist will execute a range of clinical interventions, including individual and group psychotherapy and clinical case management, and will own the documentation of these. They will also lead the use of observational assessment data to drive data-driven case conceptualization, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making for the treatment team. They will conduct psychological assessments as needed. While Social Learning Programs are a recognized evidence-based practice in and of themselves, they can also incorporate additional evidence-based practices to meet the individual needs and functioning of clients; therefore, the Psychologist is expected to stay current with existing and emerging evidence-based practices so they can be considered for implementation. Psychologists who are creative, detail-oriented, and dedicated to the delivery of evidence-based treatment would be ideally suited to this position.

Doctorate in Psychology
License eligible or licensed as a Psychologist
Training and/or experience treating individuals diagnosed with serious mental illnesses

cond_0377.intro: The Social Learning Program at [Company name masked] is the longest running program of its kind in the nation. Research has established the Social Learning Program as the ""treatment of choice"" for individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders in inpatient treatment settings. It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community.
cond_0377.responsibilities: The Social Learning Program is looking for a Psychologist with training and experience working with individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders. The Psychologist will function as an active member of an interdisciplinary treatment team. In addition to delivering milieu-based services, the Psychologist will execute a range of clinical interventions, including individual and group psychotherapy and clinical case management, and will own the documentation of these. They will also lead the use of observational assessment data to drive data-driven case conceptualization, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making for the treatment team. They will conduct psychological assessments as needed. While Social Learning Programs are a recognized evidence-based practice in and of themselves, they can also incorporate additional evidence-based practices to meet the individual needs and functioning of clients; therefore, the Psychologist is expected to stay current with existing and emerging evidence-based practices so they can be considered for implementation. Psychologists who are creative, detail-oriented, and dedicated to the delivery of evidence-based treatment would be ideally suited to this position.

cond_0464.intro: Located within the high-security [Product name masked], the Social Learning Program at [Company name masked] is the longest running program of its kind in the nation. Research has established the Social Learning Program as the ""treatment of choice"" for individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders in inpatient treatment settings. It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community. Psychologists tend to grow stronger in this work over time as they build experience with evidence-based milieu treatment and learn from working closely with interdisciplinary teams.

It is an evidence-based, highly structured, milieu-based approach to treatment consisting of a network of skills training techniques and supports based on learning theory, individually tailored to client needs and delivered by all staff within the context of a supportive, rehabilitation-oriented foundation. Together these interventions form an extremely positive teaching environment that assists clients in developing adaptive behaviors and skills relevant to successful return to the community.
cond_0641.responsibilities: The Social Learning Program is looking for a Psychologist with training and experience working with individuals diagnosed with psychotic disorders. The Psychologist will function as an active member of an interdisciplinary treatment team. In addition to providing milieu-based services, the Psychologist will utilize a range of clinical interventions, including individual and group psychotherapy and clinical case management, which they will then document. They will also utilize observational assessment data to assist the treatment team with data-driven case conceptualization, risk assessment, and clinical decision-making. They may conduct psychological assessments as needed. While Social Learning Programs are a recognized evidence-based practice in and of themselves, they can also incorporate additional evidence-based practices to meet the individual needs and functioning of clients; therefore, the Psychologist is encouraged to keep abreast of existing and emerging evidence-based practices so they can be considered for implementation. Psychologists who are creative, detail-oriented, and dedicated to the delivery of evidence-based treatment would be ideally suited to this position.
cond_0641.requirements:
Doctorate in Psychology required; advanced degree or postdoctoral training strongly preferred.
License eligible or licensed as a Psychologist, with demonstrated readiness to practice independently.
Proven track record of treating individuals diagnosed with serious mental illnesses, with deep knowledge of psychotic disorders and their clinical management.
